ut_middle_bell_tower.blurb: Middle Bell Tower is the main formation in Bell's Canyon, on the Wasatch Range's western side above the Salt Lake valley. It holds a small set of fourteen trad lines, mostly multi-pitch, with some running to several pitches. Grades start around 5.7 and the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.11, so this is a place for solid leaders rather than beginners. The tower is easy to pick out by a large right-facing corner that cuts through a pair of big roofs, with a steep smooth shield of rock on its left. The walk in is long, so plan for a full day and carry a rack.

ut_ewe_wall.blurb: Ewe Wall is a sport sector within the Lambs Knoll climbing area near St. George, in southwest Utah. Fourteen bolted lines are split between a lower tier and an upper tier that needs a little extra walking. Expect steady difficulty: a handful of 5.10s, a larger group of 5.11s, and a few 5.12s, with nothing easy. The rock is sandstone. The walls face west, so most of the area is cool through the day but this wall picks up sun by early afternoon in summer, which makes it better for cooler seasons. The other sectors of Lambs Knoll sit close by.

ut_nature_center_wall.blurb: Nature Center Wall is a quartzite cliff band on the hillside above North Ogden, on the Wasatch Front. Fourteen single-pitch routes are scattered along it, mostly bolted sport lines with a few trad climbs. The sport routes cluster in the 5.11 to 5.12 range, while the trad lines are moderate, with a couple of easier options around 5.8 and 5.9. There is no proper trail to the base, so the approach is a bit of a scramble over talus. It suits climbers who want steep, harder single pitches close to town rather than a beginner crag.
ut_nature_center_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the Ogden Nature Center trailhead in North Ogden, just north of 1100 North.
ut_nature_center_wall.approach: No built trail reaches the cliff. Go up the trails to reach the Bonneville Shoreline, then work up a line of talus to the wall.

ut_smithfield_dry_canyon_2.blurb: Smithfield Dry Canyon is a small trad crag in Cache Valley, in the northern Wasatch above the town of Smithfield. The quartzite is solid, and climbing here tends to be better than the cliff looks from below. Most routes are short trad lines of moderate difficulty, from about 5.7 to 5.10, including crack climbs and some face climbing. A handful of easy to moderate boulder problems are also logged. Descents are by rappel or an easy walk-off. It sees little traffic, which suits climbers looking for quiet traditional routes close to Logan.

vt_ship_s_prow_2.blurb: Ship's Prow is a triangular boulder with a prow-like front, beside Bolton Notch Road in the Bolton area of northern Vermont. It is one of the better-known boulder groups on this road, with fourteen problems. Most are easy to moderate, from the lowest grades up to V4, and a few harder lines reach into the upper range. It is a good stop for a mixed group, since there are plenty of lower-grade problems alongside a handful of classics. The boulder stands close to the road and is easiest to spot in leafless months.

vt_practice_slab.blurb: Practice Slab is a broad, low-angle slab on the far left side of Wheeler Mountain, in Vermont's Northeast Kingdom near Lake Willoughby. It holds fourteen routes, mostly traditionally protected, with two bolted lines. The grades are gentle: most fall around 5.6, with a few in the 5.7 to 5.8 range and one easier line near 5.4. That makes it a sensible place to learn slab technique or lead your first trad pitches before moving to the steeper cliffs on the mountain. Several of the routes carry multiple star ratings from climbers.

vt_bog_wall.blurb: Bog Wall is a small crag in the Bolton area of northern Vermont, in the Camel's Hump Forest and not far from the Winooski River valley. It has fourteen routes: mainly sport, a good number of trad lines, and one top-rope. Difficulty is mostly easy to moderate, with many climbs around 5.7 and 5.8 and a few harder ones near 5.10. That gives beginners and newer leaders somewhere friendly to work, while a few lines offer a small step up.
